easy.def: Very bad and mean.
examples: The wicked witch was mean.
A wicked king ruled.
The wicked wolf huffed and puffed.

more.def: Very bad, and doing harm on purpose.
examples: The wicked queen in the story gave the girl a poisoned apple.
A wicked king ruled the land and took the farmers' crops.
The wicked wolf tried to trick the three little pigs.

easy.def: Big from one side to the other.
examples: The river is wide.
He has a wide smile.
The road is wide.

more.def: Measuring a long way from one side to the other.
examples: The wide road had room for four cars.
The river was too wide to swim across.
She opened her eyes wide in surprise.

easy.def: To make something wider.
examples: They will widen the road.
Her eyes widened.
The river widens near the sea.

more.def: To become or to make something wider.
examples: Workers will widen the road to fit more cars.
Her eyes widened when she saw the huge cake.
The river widens as it reaches the sea.

easy.def: A woman whose husband has died.
examples: The widow lived alone.
The widow missed her husband.
A widow lives next door.

more.def: A woman whose husband has died and who has not married again.
examples: The widow lived alone in a small house.
The neighbors helped the widow with her garden.
The widow kept her husband's photo on the shelf.

easy.def: A woman who is married to someone.
examples: He kissed his wife.
The farmer and his wife work.
Her wife is a nurse.

more.def: A woman who is married to another person.
examples: The baker and his wife open the shop at six each morning.
My uncle's wife is my aunt.
His wife grows tomatoes in the garden behind the house.

easy.def: A covering of fake hair for the head.
examples: The clown wore a wig.
The wig is red.
I put on a wig.

more.def: A covering of hair, made of real or fake hair, that is worn on the head.
examples: The clown wore a bright red wig.
The judge wore a white wig in the old days.
I put on a wig for the costume party.

easy.def: To move with short, quick moves from side to side.
examples: I wiggle my toes.
The worm wiggled.
The puppy wiggles when it is happy.

more.def: To move from side to side or up and down with small, quick moves.
examples: I wiggled my toes in the sand.
The worm wiggled across the sidewalk.
My loose tooth wiggled when I touched it with my tongue.

easy.def: A small, quick move from side to side.
examples: The puppy did a wiggle.
Give a little wiggle.
A wiggle in the chair.

more.def: A short, quick movement from side to side.
examples: The puppy gave a happy wiggle when it saw me.
She did a little wiggle to the music.
With a wiggle, the worm slid into the ground.

easy.def: Living in nature, not with people.
examples: A wolf is a wild animal.
Wild birds sing in the trees.
A wild horse ran free.

more.def: Living or growing in nature without being cared for by people.
examples: We picked wild berries along the trail.
Wild horses still live on the island.
The garden grew wild after no one looked after it.

easy.def: A wild animal like a big cat.
examples: A wildcat hid in the trees.
The wildcat has sharp claws.
We read about a wildcat.

more.def: A kind of wild cat that is bigger than a house cat, such as a bobcat or a lynx.
examples: A wildcat crept silently through the tall grass at night.
The bobcat is a wildcat with a short tail and tufted ears.
Wildcats hunt mice and rabbits in the forest.

easy.def: A wild place where few people live.
examples: We hiked in the wilderness.
The wilderness is quiet.
A bear lives in the wilderness.

more.def: A large, wild area of land that has not been changed by people.
examples: We hiked through the wilderness for three days.
Bears and wolves live in the wilderness of the north.
The explorers crossed a wide, empty wilderness.

easy.def: Wild animals and plants that live in nature.
examples: We watched the wildlife.
The park has lots of wildlife.
Protect the wildlife.

more.def: Wild animals and plants that live in nature, not in homes or on farms.
examples: We saw deer, foxes and owls on the wildlife walk.
The park protects the wildlife that lives there.
Wildlife needs clean water and safe places to live.

easy.def: In a wild or out-of-control way.
examples: The dog barked wildly.
The crowd cheered wildly.
The wind blew wildly.

more.def: In a way that is not controlled or calm.
examples: The dog barked wildly at the door.
The wildly spinning top fell off the table.
The wind blew wildly through the trees.

easy.def: A word used to show something is going to happen.
examples: I will go to bed soon.
It will snow tomorrow.
She will be here at six.

more.def: A word used to say what is going to happen in the future, or to say that someone is willing to do something.
examples: Our class will visit the science museum next week.
I will help you carry those groceries.
Spring will come after the long winter.

easy.def: Ready to do something.
examples: I am willing to help.
She is willing to share.
Are you willing to try?

more.def: Ready and happy to do something if asked.
examples: I am willing to help with the dishes.
Are you willing to share your snack?
She was willing to walk the dog in the rain.

easy.def: Being happy to do something.
examples: She showed willingness to help.
His willingness was clear.
We thanked her for her willingness.

more.def: The feeling of being ready and glad to do something.
examples: Her willingness to help made the job easy.
He showed his willingness to share his toys.
The team's willingness to practice paid off.

easy.def: A tree with long, thin branches that hang down.
examples: The willow grew by the pond.
The willow droops.
We sat under the willow.

more.def: A tree with long, bendy branches and narrow leaves that grows near water.
examples: A willow grew beside the river.
The willow's branches swept the ground.
We sat in the shade of the willow.

easy.def: To get weak and soft from heat or no water.
examples: The flowers wilted.
Plants wilt without water.
The lettuce wilted.

more.def: To droop and become weak, as a plant does when it does not get enough water or is too hot.
examples: The flowers wilted in the hot sun before we could water them.
Plants wilt when they do not get enough water.
I felt myself wilt in the heat of the afternoon.

easy.def: To come in first in a game.
examples: I want to win.
Our team won.
She wins every race.

more.def: To be first or best in a game or contest, or to get a prize.
examples: Our class won the spelling contest after weeks of practice.
The runner won the race by a few seconds.
He hopes to win a ribbon at the fair.

easy.def: Air that moves.
examples: The wind blows.
Wind lifted the kite.
A cold wind came.

more.def: Air that is moving, often strong enough to feel.
examples: The wind blew the leaves across the yard.
A strong wind knocked over the chairs.
Sailboats move with the wind.

easy.def: To turn around and around.
examples: Wind the string.
She winds the clock.
He wound the yarn into a ball.

more.def: To turn or wrap something around and around.
examples: She wound the yarn into a ball.
Wind the knob on the music box.
Wind the rope around the post.

easy.def: A tall building with big blades that spin in the wind.
examples: The windmill spins.
We saw a windmill in Holland.
The windmill grinds grain.

more.def: A tall building or machine with large blades that are turned by the wind and used to grind grain or pump water.
examples: The big blades of the windmill turned slowly in the breeze.
A windmill pumped water from the well for the farm.
The old windmill ground wheat into flour.

easy.def: Glass in a wall that lets in light.
examples: Open the window.
I look out the window.
The window is clean.

more.def: An opening in a wall filled with glass, which lets in light and lets you see outside.
examples: We watched snow fall outside the window.
She opened the window to let in fresh air.
A bird tapped on the window.

easy.def: The big glass window at the front of a car.
examples: The windshield is clean.
Rain hit the windshield.
A bug is on the windshield.

more.def: The large glass window at the front of a car or truck.
examples: The wipers cleared the rain from the windshield.
A bug splattered on the windshield.
Dad scraped the ice off the windshield.

easy.def: With a lot of wind.
examples: It is a windy day.
The windy weather blew my hat.
The hill was windy.

more.def: Having a lot of wind blowing.
examples: It was a windy day, perfect for flying kites.
The windy weather blew leaves all over the yard.
We held onto our hats on the windy hilltop.

easy.def: The part of a bird that it flies with.
examples: The bird flapped its wing.
Bats have wings.
A bird has two wings.

more.def: A part of a bird, bat or insect that it uses to fly.
examples: The bird flapped its wings and took off.
Butterflies have colorful wings.
A bat folds its wings when it rests.

easy.def: A part of an airplane.
examples: The plane's wing is long.
A wing holds the plane up.
The plane has two wings.

more.def: A flat part that sticks out from the side of an airplane and helps it fly.
examples: The plane's wing glinted in the sun.
Each wing holds a fuel tank.
The wings of a jet are long and strong.

easy.def: Having wings.
examples: The winged horse flew.
A winged bug landed.
The winged cat is in the story.

more.def: Having wings.
examples: A winged horse flew through the sky in the myth.
A small winged insect landed on my arm.
The winged seeds spun down from the maple tree.

easy.def: How far a bird's or plane's wings reach, from tip to tip.
examples: The eagle has a long wingspan.
The plane's wingspan is wide.
A wingspan can be huge.

more.def: The distance from the tip of one wing to the tip of the other when they are spread out.
examples: The eagle has a wingspan of six feet.
The airplane's wingspan was longer than a bus.
The butterfly's wingspan was only two inches.

easy.def: To close one eye quickly.
examples: I wink.
She winked at me.
He winked and smiled.

more.def: To close and open one eye quickly, often as a signal.
examples: She winked at me across the room.
He winked and gave a smile.
The owl seemed to wink.

easy.def: A person who wins.
examples: The winner got a prize.
She is the winner.
Cheer for the winner.

more.def: A person or team that wins a game or contest.
examples: The winner of the race got a gold medal.
Our class was the winner of the spelling bee.
The crowd cheered for the winner.

easy.def: The coldest time of the year.
examples: It snows in winter.
We wear coats in winter.
Winter comes after fall.

more.def: The coldest season of the year, between fall and spring.
examples: Many bears sleep through the winter.
Days are short and nights are long in winter.
We went sledding on the first snowy day of winter.

easy.def: Cold and like winter.
examples: It was a wintry day.
The wintry wind blew.
A wintry scene.

more.def: Cold, snowy or icy, like winter.
examples: It was a wintry day with snow and a cold wind.
We walked through the wintry woods.
A wintry mix of rain and snow fell.

easy.def: To rub something to make it clean or dry.
examples: Please wipe the table.
I wipe my feet on the mat.
She wiped her hands on a towel.

more.def: To clean or dry something by rubbing it with a cloth or your hand.
examples: He wiped the steam off the bathroom mirror.
The waiter wiped the counter after we finished our lunch.
Wipe the dust from the shelf with a soft cloth.

easy.def: A thin metal thread.
examples: The wire is thin.
A wire runs to the lamp.
Birds sat on the wire.

more.def: A thin, bendable piece of metal like a thread.
examples: A wire runs from the plug to the lamp.
Birds sat in a row on the wire.
The fence was made of wire.

easy.def: Working without wires.
examples: My headphones are wireless.
We use wireless internet.
A wireless mouse.

more.def: Not needing wires to connect or work.
examples: My headphones are wireless, so I can move around.
We use a wireless connection for our laptop.
The wireless doorbell rang in the kitchen.

easy.def: The wires that carry electricity in a building.
examples: The wiring is old.
The wiring is in the wall.
Dad fixed the wiring.

more.def: The set of wires that carry electricity through a building, a car or a machine.
examples: The electrician checked the old wiring in the attic.
The wiring in the walls carries power to every outlet.
A mouse chewed through the wiring in the car.

easy.def: Knowing what is good and right to do.
examples: Grandma has a lot of wisdom.
The old owl in the story has wisdom.
There is wisdom in that old saying.

more.def: Good sense and judgment that comes from knowledge and experience.
examples: The old story is full of wisdom about being kind.
People came from far away to hear the teacher's wisdom.
With age comes wisdom, my grandmother says.

easy.def: Knowing a lot and making good choices.
examples: My grandpa is wise.
The wise old owl gave good advice.
It is wise to wear a coat in the cold.

more.def: Having good judgment and knowing what is right, often from experience.
examples: It was wise to bring a raincoat on such a cloudy day.
The wise queen listened before she decided.
He made a wise choice to save his money.

easy.def: To want something very much.
examples: I wish for a puppy.
She wished it would snow.
We wish you well.

more.def: To want something to happen, often something that may not be possible.
examples: I wish I could fly like a bird.
She wished upon a star before bed.
We wished that the summer would last longer.

easy.def: Something you want very much.
examples: Make a wish.
My wish came true.
Her wish is a pony.

more.def: A strong feeling of wanting something to happen.
examples: Blow out the candles and make a wish.
His wish was to see the ocean one day.
They did their best to grant her wish.

easy.def: Thin and light.
examples: The clouds are wispy.
Wispy hair blew in the wind.
A wispy tail.

more.def: Thin, light and soft, in small, delicate strands.
examples: Wispy clouds floated across the blue sky.
The baby had soft, wispy hair that stuck up in all directions.
A wispy thread of smoke rose from the candle.

easy.def: The ability to say clever, funny things.
examples: He has a quick wit.
Her wit made us laugh.
The joke showed his wit.

more.def: The ability to say clever and funny things quickly.
examples: He has a quick wit and makes us all laugh.
Her wit made the party fun.
The writer is known for her sharp wit.

easy.def: A woman in stories who has magic powers.
examples: The witch rode a broom.
The witch stirred her pot.
The witch cast a spell.

more.def: In stories, a woman who uses magic spells.
examples: The witch in the story stirred a bubbling pot.
She dressed as a witch for Halloween.
The witch flew on her broom.

easy.def: Magic that witches do in stories.
examples: The story had witchcraft.
The witch used witchcraft.
The tale was full of witchcraft.

more.def: The use of magic spells and powers, especially by witches in stories.
examples: In the fairy tale, the old woman used witchcraft to turn the frog into a prince.
Long ago, people told stories about witchcraft around the fire.
The book was filled with spells and witchcraft.

easy.def: A word that shows two things go together.
examples: I play with my friend.
Cut it with scissors.
She came with her dad.

more.def: A word used to show that people or things are together, or to show the tool or thing that is used.
examples: We walked to the park with our grandfather.
He painted the picture with a thin brush.
A sandwich with cheese and tomato is my favorite lunch.

easy.def: To take something out or back.
examples: I withdraw money from the bank.
The team withdrew from the game.
He withdrew his hand.

more.def: To take something out, or to pull back or leave.
examples: She withdrew money from her savings.
The team withdrew from the race when its runner was hurt.
He withdrew his hand from the hot stove.

easy.def: Taking something out or away.
examples: Mom made a withdrawal.
The withdrawal of the army.
A withdrawal is taking out.

more.def: The act of taking something out, or pulling away from a place.
examples: He made a withdrawal at the bank.
The withdrawal of the troops took a week.
She was sad about her friend's withdrawal from the club.

easy.def: Inside of something.
examples: The note is within the box.
Stay within the lines.
The park is within walking distance.

more.def: Inside something, or not farther than a certain distance or time.
examples: The school is within a mile of our house.
Color within the lines.
The doctor will see you within an hour.

easy.def: Not having something.
examples: I went without a coat.
Tea without sugar.
Do not go without me.

more.def: Not having or not using something.
examples: We cannot live without water.
She left the house without her umbrella.
He solved the puzzle without any help.

easy.def: To not break under strong force.
examples: The house can withstand wind.
The bridge withstood the storm.
It can withstand rain.

more.def: To stay strong against something, such as wind, heat or hard use, without being damaged.
examples: The strong house can withstand the winds of a big storm.
The bridge has withstood floods for a hundred years.
These boots can withstand rain and snow.

easy.def: A person who sees something happen.
examples: A witness saw the accident.
The witness told the police.
She was a witness to the race.

more.def: A person who sees an event happen and can tell others about it.
examples: A witness told the officer what she saw.
He was a witness when the old tree fell.
Several witnesses saw the rainbow.

easy.def: To see something happen.
examples: We witnessed a rainbow.
She witnessed the race.
They witnessed the parade.

more.def: To see an event happen.
examples: Thousands of people witnessed the rocket launch.
We witnessed a beautiful sunset.
Anyone who witnessed the accident should tell the police.

easy.def: The ability to think quickly.
examples: Use your wits to solve it.
She kept her wits.
He used his wits.

more.def: The ability to think clearly and quickly, especially when something unexpected happens.
examples: The little fox used its wits to escape from the farmer's garden.
She kept her wits when the lights went out and found the flashlight.
He had to use his wits to solve the riddle.

easy.def: Clever and funny.
examples: She is a witty girl.
A witty joke.
He made a witty remark.

more.def: Clever and funny in what you say.
examples: She is witty and always makes us laugh.
He made a witty remark that made the class smile.
A witty poem is full of clever words.

easy.def: A man in stories who does magic.
examples: The wizard waved a wand.
The wizard wore a tall hat.
The wizard cast a spell.

more.def: A man in stories who has magic powers.
examples: The wizard waved his wand and the cup flew.
The old wizard lived in a tower.
In the story, the wizard helped the lost boy.
